prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a room corner bounded by a bright, very close wall on the left (about 0.3–0.6 m away in frames 1–4, shifting to the upper right in frame 5 as the camera wearer turns and moves around the highchair) and a darker recessed corner with a small black table, router, and curtains about 1.5–2.2 m ahead and to the right. In the lower foreground, a baby in a highchair is positioned below the camera wearer at roughly 0.5–0.9 m distance (within the camera wearer's arm's reach, with the wearer's hands gripping and pushing the highchair back in frame 4), while in frame 5 a second older child stands on the floor to the left of the highchair at about 1.0–1.3 m away, within arm's reach of the highchair tray and about 0.4 m from the baby. Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer steps around and behind the highchair (causing the baby's head to drop partly out of the lower frame edge in frame 4 while the corner table approaches to roughly 1.2 m), and in frame 5 pivots clockwise so the highchair moves to the lower right and the standing child comes into view on the left. The depth map makes the continuous 3D geometry of the featureless wall, the vertical elevation difference between the elevated highchair seat and the recessed floor, and the exact silhouette of the router antennas on the dark table much clearer than in the dimly lit RGB image. However, it looks unreliable in the bright sunlit doorway gap on the far right of frame 1 (which is rendered pitch-black as if infinitely far) and flattens the depth gradient along the oblique wall plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground entities in only three of the five frames, showing the baby and highchair merged together at about 0.5–0.9 m below and in front of the camera wearer in frames 1, 3, and 5, and parts of the standing child on the left at 1.0–1.3 m in frame 5. In frame 1 the baby (facing toward the camera wearer's left/back and looking away) and highchair are combined into a single pink 'person' mask; in frame 3 the highchair frame around the baby is mislabelled as a green 'bowl' mask with an unsegmented hole where the baby's head and torso sit; and in frame 5 multiple overlapping 'person' masks cover the highchair tray (pink), the baby's arm and highchair back on the lower right (cyan), and the standing child and background chair on the left (brown and yellow-green). These masks reflect the highchair shifting from the lower left-center (frame 1) toward the bottom right (frames 3 and 5) within arm's reach of the camera wearer, while the standing child in frame 5 faces right toward the highchair with both hands resting on the tray edge and looking slightly upward toward the camera wearer. While the segmentation map highlights the outer contour of the curved highchair tray and backrest in frames 3 and 5, it adds almost no spatial detail that is hard to see in RGB alone. Overall, the map is highly unreliable: it completely misses all people and objects in frames 2 and 4, omits the corner table, router, and curtains across all frames, and severely misclassifies and fragments the highchair, background chair, and children into overlapping 'person' and 'bowl' masks.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body skeletons on a black background for only three frames, detecting the seated baby in the lower foreground (about 0.6–0.8 m below the camera wearer) in frames 2 and 3, and the standing child on the left (about 1.0–1.3 m away, roughly 0.4 m from the baby) in frame 5. In frames 2 and 3, the baby's head and upper-body keypoints show the baby seated inside the highchair, facing away and toward the camera wearer's left/upper-left (looking toward the backrest rather than at the camera wearer) with bent arms resting within reach of the highchair backrest and tray as the camera wearer circles counter-clockwise around the chair. In frame 5, the skeleton switches to the standing child on the left of the highchair, capturing their head, torso, and both outstretched arms reaching forward and right to grip the highchair tray edge while their head faces right and tilts slightly up toward the camera wearer. The pose map clarifies the exact head orientation (eyes, nose, and ears keypoints) and shoulder-to-elbow angles of the baby under the steep overhead viewing angle in frames 2–3 and the bi-manual reach of the standing child in frame 5, which are somewhat obscured by motion blur and shadow in RGB. However, the map is unreliable where it completely misses the baby in frames 1, 4 (where the baby is largely occluded by the highchair back and bottom frame edge), and 5, fails to detect the camera wearer's own hands touching the chair in frame 4 and feet in frame 4, and produces no magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
